seat_A_anchor.note: the ladder's revision anchor; carried at FULL length after qa-lane-engineer pointed out that my earlier record held only the 16-hex prefix — a truncated hash is the same defect class as a pin without its moment

seat_B_anchor.fold: sha256 over sorted lines `relpath + "\0" + sha256(file)`, LF-joined WITH a trailing LF, under BYTE collation (LC_ALL=C / code-unit order)
seat_B_anchor.fold_precision_found_by_reproduction: the trailing LF is load-bearing: LF-joined without it gives 570177010ac1f15983654edebd4e2dde7b4b26237be3707c051f542b909624b7, and NUL-joining gives 0e8d236c8c57e89e13bb288b8ed2f6fbf8889348a8b019c60beed36597657756 — only the trailing-LF variant reproduces the peer's digest
seat_B_anchor.fold_collation_matters: the packing seat first computed the fold with a locale-aware `sort` and got d30f7d19… (288 positions differ from byte order); under byte/LC_ALL=C collation it reproduces 4131137d… — so the spec needs THREE parts: algorithm (per-file sha256 over sorted rel+NUL+hash records), encoding (LF-joined, trailing LF included), and COLLATION (byte order, not locale order). My own reproduction used JS Array.sort() (code-unit order) and matched the byte-collation value, which is the independent confirmation of that clause.
seat_B_anchor.fold_shell_twin: R=dist/mpd-package; ( cd "$R" && find . -type f -print0 | LC_ALL=C sort -z | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do printf '%s\0%s\n' "${f#./}" "$(sha256sum "$f" | cut -d' ' -f1)"; done ) | sha256sum
